configuration.ignoredFileGlobs.descripti: Glob-like file patterns to ignore entirely in Code Block Review. Ignored files do not enter auto/manual baselines, do not start capture, and do not appear in review lists. Examples: `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `**/pnpm-lock.yaml`, `**/*.snap`. Recommended for lockfiles, snapshots, generated files, and vendored assets.
configuration.showBlockBadges.descriptio: Show inline ADDED, REPLACED, DELETED, and KEPT badges before highlighted review blocks. Disabled by default to keep editor decorations compact.
configuration.autoCapture.enabled.descri: Enable always-on automatic review capture while no session is active. Auto mode continuously watches for short bursts of large or bulk edits and never overrides an active manual session. Recommended default: enabled unless you only want manual review sessions.
Choose which supported editor events refresh the always-on auto-capture baseline while auto mode is enabled. Recommended default: keep both. If you feel baseline refresh is too frequent, remove `activeEditorChange` first.
Refresh the background auto-capture baseline when the VS Code window regains focus.
Refresh the background auto-capture baseline when the active code editor changes.
configuration.autoCapture.scope.descript: Controls how much of a large workspace auto-capture preloads into the idle baseline. Default `touchedProjects` balances coverage and startup cost; use `workspace` for the most conservative accuracy.
configuration.autoCapture.scope.workspac: Capture the idle baseline from the entire VS Code/Cursor workspace. This is the most conservative option for accuracy.
configuration.autoCapture.scope.activePr: Capture the idle baseline from the nearest detected project root for the active editor. Use this for very large workspaces when you usually work in one subproject at a time.
configuration.autoCapture.scope.touchedP: Capture the idle baseline from the active project plus project roots touched by recent evidence. This is the default balance for large multi-project workspaces and still keeps exact touched files as evidence.
configuration.autoCapture.projectRootMar: Marker files or directories used to infer the nearest project root for scoped auto-capture baselines. Add team-specific markers such as `.project-root` when a workspace contains many subprojects.
configuration.autoCapture.baselineRefres: Minimum cooldown between auto-capture baseline refreshes triggered by focus/editor-change events once a baseline already exists. `0` disables throttling. Recommended default: `10`. If you still see frequent refreshes, try `15-30`.
configuration.autoCapture.captureIdleSec: How long an automatic capture session waits without new edits before it stops actively recording and offers you a manual review window. Balanced default: `4`. More responsive: `2-3`. More conservative for long AI runs: `6-10`.
configuration.autoCapture.reviewOfferSec: After automatic capture goes idle, how long Code Block Review waits for you to manually open review before silently syncing the current workspace into the baseline and leaving capture mode. Recommended default: `120`. Set to `0` to wait indefinitely until you review or skip manually; large sessions may keep baseline snapshots and review blocks in memory until handled.
configuration.autoCapture.observationWin: How long the auto-capture heuristic observes early edits before deciding whether they look like AI/external bulk edits. A longer window gives later edits more time to join the same burst; a shorter window decides sooner.
configuration.autoCapture.burstEventWind: A short event-density window used as an assist signal for machine-like edit speed. It does not trigger capture by itself; instead, high event density can slightly relax multi-file or burst-line thresholds inside the same observation window.
configuration.autoCapture.largeChangeLin: A single edit touching at least this many lines is treated as a strong AI/external signal. Balanced default: `8`. Aggressive capture: `4-6`. Conservative capture: `12-20`. Lower values trigger more easily.
configuration.autoCapture.largeChangeCha: A single edit changing at least this many characters is treated as a strong AI/external signal. Balanced default: `200`. Aggressive capture: `80-160`. Conservative capture: `240-400`. Lower values trigger more easily.
configuration.autoCapture.multiFileMinFi: If early edits touch at least this many files within the observation window, they are more likely to be treated as AI/external edits. Balanced default: `2`. Aggressive capture: keep `2`. Conservative capture: `3`.
configuration.autoCapture.multiFileMinLi: When multiple files are touched, the combined changed-line count must reach this threshold before auto-capture starts. Balanced default: `8`. Aggressive capture: `4-6`. Conservative capture: `12-20`.
configuration.autoCapture.burstMinEvents: How many edit events inside the short burst-event window are treated as a strong rapid-edit assist signal. This no longer triggers capture by itself; it only helps relax nearby multi-file or burst-line thresholds. The default `10` within `500ms` aims to stay above normal typing speed.
How many unique touched lines within the observation window a burst needs before auto-capture starts. Repeated edits on the same line are merged instead of being counted again. Balanced default: `18`. Aggressive capture: `8-12`. Conservative capture: `24-40`.
configuration.profiler.enabled.descripti: Enable Code Block Review profiler logging in the Output Channel. Keep disabled during normal use to avoid extra logging overhead.
